Proposed screen map (9 screens)
#	Screen	What it does
1	Insights (home)	Revenue cards (today/week/month), Avg. Transaction Value, Revenue Breakdown — by category, by product, by payment method. Charts + trends.
2	Transactions	Single ledger of every money event: sale payments, invoice payments, refunds. Filter by date/type/status. Tap for full detail.
3	Customers	Add/edit customers (individual vs. corporate), phone/email/address, purchase history, outstanding credit balance.
4	Receipts	Auto-numbered proof-of-payment docs, generated when money is received. Preview, share (PDF/WhatsApp), reprint.
5	Invoice	Bill-now-pay-later documents for corporate clients. Track Unpaid → Partial → Paid; payment posts to Transactions and issues a Receipt.
6	MILS	Maintenance Information Log Sheet — per-equipment records: item/serial, client & location, service date, action (refill/inspection/installation), technician, next-due date with overdue alerts. Can generate an invoice for the job.
7	Sales	The selling screen (POS): pick customer → add items from stock → discount → payment method → complete. Auto-deducts stock, creates Transaction + Receipt (or Invoice if on credit).
8	Stock	Product list with quantities, cost/selling price, low-stock alerts & reorder levels, stock adjustments (goods received, damage, correction).
9	Summary	Period report (daily/weekly/monthly/custom): totals, profit estimate, top products, stock valuation, outstanding invoices — exportable/shareable.
How they connect: Sale → Transaction → Receipt, Invoice → Payment → Receipt, Stock feeds Sales, MILS job can become an Invoice.

Proposed data entities
Product — id, name, category, cost price, selling price, quantity, reorder level
Customer — name, type (individual/corporate), phone, email, address, balance
Sale — date, customer, items (product + qty + unit price), discount, payment method, status
Transaction — type (sale payment / invoice payment / refund), amount, method, date, link to sale or invoice
Receipt / Invoice — sequential numbering (e.g. MTK-REC-0001, MTK-INV-0001), line items, totals, status
MaintenanceLog (MILS) — equipment ID/type, client, location, action performed, technician, date, next-due date
StockAdjustment — reason (restock/damage/correction), qty change, date
Proposed tech stack
Flutter (Dart), Material 3, ₦ currency formatting
Drift (SQLite) — offline-first local database, ideal for the reporting queries Insights/Summary need
Riverpod for state management, fl_chart for graphs, pdf + printing packages for receipts/invoices
Designed so a cloud sync layer (Firebase/Supabase) can be added later without rewrites

Master Technical Blueprint: M-Tek Document Generation Module

Project Scope

Build a document rendering and sharing module in Flutter that dynamically maps transactional entries to match physical corporate forms—specifically the Maintenance Information Log Sheet (MILS), Payment Receipt, and Sales Invoice—and exports them as unalterable PDF files for instant distribution via WhatsApp or email.

Tech Stack & Dependencies

Framework: Flutter (Dart)

PDF Engine: pdf and printing packages

File Management: path_provider (for local caching)

Sharing Utility: share_plus (for multi-channel sharing)

Document Layout Blueprints & Data Schemas

Maintenance Information Log Sheet (MILS)
Header Data: Company branding (M-Tek Fire & Safety Ltd, RC: 1082534, Address, Contact info), MILS No, LPO No, Entry Date, Collection Date, and Next Service Date.

Grid Architecture: Two primary tabular sections. The first maps out weight categories from 1kg up to 75kg. The second section maps specific technical components including Nipple, Horn, Hose, Manometre, Valve, Strap, Label, Lever, Powder, Pull Pin, and Cartridge.

Footer Metadata: Prepared by, Approved by, Customer/Client assent blocks, and statutory maintenance conditions.

Payment Receipt
Header Data: Document title Payment Receipt, IRN field, Receipt Serial Number, and Date.

Fields: Customer Name, Address, Phone Number, "The Sum of" (amount in words), and "Being Payment for".

Payment Method Checkboxes: Cash, Cheque, Transfer, and POS.

Footer Metadata: "For: M-Tek Fire & Safety Ltd", "For: Customer's Client", and standard non-returnable goods disclaimer.

Sales Invoice / Commercial Form
Header Data: Checkboxes for Way Bill, Pro-Former, Service Invoice, and Sales Invoice, alongside Serial Number, Phone, Address, Customer Name, MILS No, Receipt No, LPO No, and Date.

Itemized Ledger Table: Columns for S/NO, Description, Qty, Rate, and Amount (₦ / K).

Financial Summary Block: 7.5% VAT, Grand Total, Advance Payment, Balance Payment, Amount in Words, and sign-off blocks (Prepared by, Approved by, Customer/Client).

Execution Logic & Workflow Architecture

Document Selector State: Provide a UI controller allowing the user to select the active document type (mils, receipt, or invoice) before data entry.

Dynamic PDF Painter: Implement conditional layout builders using the pdf package that swap out table grids, field alignments, and corporate headers based on the active document type selected.

Export & Dispatch Pipeline: Capture the generated PDF document stream, write it to a temporary local directory with a unique timestamped filename using path_provider, and pass the file path into share_plus to route the PDF directly to WhatsApp or email clients.

Master Technical Blueprint: M-Tek Document Generation Module (Part 2 — Advanced Implementation & UI Architecture)
Project Scope
Expand the core document rendering and sharing module into a fully realized, state-managed Flutter application interface. This upgrade implements dynamic form controllers, real-time calculation logic, and responsive screen layouts specifically tailored for generating, previewing, and instantly exporting M-Tek Fire & Safety Ltd documents (MILS, Payment Receipt, and Sales Invoice).
Tech Stack & Architecture Additions
 * State Management: Flutter StatefulWidget combined with modular controllers for real-time form inputs and calculations.
 * Layout Engine: Responsive Expanded, ListView, and custom Table widgets mimicking physical paper dimensions.
 * Export Pipeline: pdf, path_provider, and share_plus integrated into a unified background service.
UI Form Components & State Logic
 * 1. Document Type Switcher (TabBar / Segmented Control)
   * A top-level selection bar allowing seamless switching between Invoice, Receipt, and MILS states.
   * Dynamically swaps out the form input fields and underlying data model without losing context.
 * 2. Dynamic Itemized Ledger Form (For Invoices & MILS)
   * Input Rows: Dynamic rows for Description, Quantity, and Unit Rate.
   * Live Calculations: Automatic multiplication of Qty × Rate, calculation of 7.5% VAT, and immediate updating of the Grand Total, Advance Payment, and Balance Payment fields.
 * 3. Component & Weight Grid Matrix (For MILS)
   * Weight Checkboxes / Fields: Interactive grid cells mapping out equipment weights from 1kg to 75kg.
   * Technical Part Checklists: Toggle switches or text inputs for tracking individual components: Nipple, Horn, Hose, Manometre, Valve, Strap, Label, Lever, Powder, Pull Pin, and Cartridge.
 * 4. Financial & Customer Metadata Form (For Receipts & Invoices)
   * Text fields for Customer Name, Address, Phone Number, and "The Sum of / Amount in Words".
   * Payment method selection toggles (Cash, Cheque, Transfer, POS) updating the receipt state instantly.
Execution & Integration Pipeline
 * Validation Check: Verify that all mandatory metadata fields (Customer Name, Date, and at least one line item or weight metric) are populated before generation.
 * Asynchronous PDF Build: Pass the active form state model into the respective PDF generator layout engine to compile the byte stream.
 * Cache & Dispatch Execution: Save the rendered document locally using a unique timestamp identifier (mtek_invoice_[timestamp].pdf), initialize the native share sheet, and attach a pre-formatted message body for direct delivery via WhatsApp or email.

Master Technical Blueprint: M-Tek Document Generation Module (Part 3 — Optimization, Error Handling & Advanced Production Features)
Project Scope
Finalize the architecture of the M-Tek document generation system by establishing production-grade error handling, secure local storage persistence, custom typography scaling, and offline-first queue management for seamless field and office usage.
Core Technical Enhancements
 * 1. Offline-First Storage & Document History
   * Local Database (isar or sqflite): Store a local cache of all generated Invoices, Receipts, and MILS documents with unique serial numbers (e.g., MILS No, IRN, LPO No) so past transactions can be viewed, reprinted, or re-shared without an active internet connection.
   * Auto-Incrementing Serial Tracking: Implement a local counter service to automatically sequence serial numbers for each document type to prevent duplicate entries.
 * 2. Advanced PDF Rendering & Styling Engine
   * Exact Physical Layout Mapping: Fine-tune pw.Table cell widths, borders, and font weights to mirror the physical multi-colored corporate carbon-copy books of M-Tek Fire & Safety Ltd.
   * Dynamic Multi-Page Flow: Implement automatic page-breaking logic (pw.MultiPage) for large inventory lists or extensive maintenance logs to prevent text clipping or overflow.
   * Custom Branding Assets: Embed official corporate logo assets directly into the pdf generator header alongside statutory details (RC: 1082534, office addresses, and contact numbers).
 * 3. Robust Error Handling & Edge Case Management
   * Storage Permission Guards: Handle runtime storage exceptions gracefully on Android/iOS when writing temporary files to the cache directory.
   * Empty State Validation: Block PDF generation and display inline UI validation errors if critical fields (such as Customer Name or total amounts) are left blank.
   * Fallback Share Mechanism: If the native share sheet fails or encounters an unsupported MIME type, automatically fall back to saving the PDF directly to device downloads with a notification toast.
 * 4. Streamlined Sharing & Messaging Templates
   * Pre-Formatted Message Generator: Automatically construct a professional message body when sharing via WhatsApp or email (e.g., "Good day [Customer Name], please find attached your official Maintenance Information Log Sheet (MILS) from M-Tek Fire & Safety Ltd.").
   * Direct URI Launching: Provide optional direct deep-linking via url_launcher to push PDFs straight to specific client phone numbers or email addresses stored in the app's customer directory.

Master Technical Blueprint: M-Tek Document Generation Module (Part 4 — Deployment, Automated Backup & Maintenance Operations)
Project Scope
Establish the final deployment, cloud synchronization, automated data backup, and long-term maintenance architecture for the M-Tek document generation system to ensure data integrity across field tablets and office workstations.

   * Remote Document Ledger: Automatically back up all generated transaction records (Invoices, Receipts, MILS logs) to a secure PostgreSQL database via Supabase as soon as an internet connection is established.
   * Customer Directory Database: Maintain a synchronized list of recurring clients, phone numbers, and addresses to enable auto-complete when generating new documents in the field.
 * 2. Automated Backup & Recovery Pipeline
   * Local-to-Cloud Queue: Implement an offline sync worker that stores un-synced transactions locally and pushes them to the cloud repository once connectivity returns.
   * Periodic Export Archives: Provide an admin-level feature to export the entire transaction ledger and PDF archive into a compressed .zip package for safe off-site storage.
 * 3. Role-Based Access & Security Controls
   * Authentication Guards: Secure administrative configurations, company profile edits, and tax/VAT settings behind a secure authentication wall using Supabase Auth.
   * Audit Logging: Track document creation timestamps, modification history, and user IDs to maintain strict accountability across workshop operations.
 * 4. Post-Deployment Maintenance & Analytics
   * Crash Reporting & Diagnostics: Integrate lightweight error tracking to monitor PDF rendering exceptions or share-sheet failures in live field environments.
   * Version Control & Over-the-Air Updates: Structure the application codebase for continuous integration, ensuring smooth rollouts of new statutory requirements or template tweaks.

Future<void> _captureSignature(ValueChanged<String> onSaved, String label) async {
  await showModalBottomSheet<void>(
    context: context,
    builder: (_) => Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
      child: Column(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min, children: [
        Text(label, style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.w700)),
        const SizedBox(height: 12),
        SignaturePad(onDone: (bytes) {
          if (bytes != null) {
            onSaved('data:image/png;base64,${base64Encode(bytes)}');
          }
          Navigator.of(context).pop();  // careful: context inside builder
        }),
      ]),
    ),
  );
  setState(() {});
}

The click does NOT switch posMethod! Chip click runs posMethod='credit';render() — but the re-rendered chip is not active. Why? jsdom inline onclick executes in global scope: posMethod='credit' — assigns to... window.posMethod? NO — inline handlers compile with document scope chain: posMethod resolves via the scope chain to the global object (window). The module's let posMethod is NOT on window (script evaluated with let → script scope). So the inline handler created a NEW window-global posMethod = 'credit' while the module's let posMethod stays 'cash'!

How did this EVER work in the browser? In the browser, app.js is a classic script — top-level let posMethod creates a script-scoped binding in the global lexical environment — inline onclick handlers DO see the global lexical environment! (Inline event handlers compile with a scope chain ending at global — including let/const declarative record.) So in a real browser it works. In JSDOM's inline handler compilation... it should also work the same way. But here app.js was evaluated via window.eval(js) — eval code has its own declarative environment for let/const! So let posMethod inside eval is eval-scoped, NOT global-lexical. Inline handlers can't see it; assignment creates window.posMethod.

So this is a JSDOM artifact: module vars invisible to inline handlers when eval'd. But the smoke tests passed before (posMethod default cash — the old smoke never switched method via chip!). The old invoice test used seeded invoice. So this never got exercised.

All interactive functions used are window-assigned. The chip inline posMethod='credit';render() relies on lexical globals — broken under eval.*

Future<void> attachMilsPhotos(String logId, List<String> dataUrls) async {
  if (dataUrls.isEmpty) return;
  milsPhotos.putIfAbsent(logId, () => <String>[]).addAll(dataUrls);
  final all = <Map<String, dynamic>>[];
  milsPhotos.forEach((log, urls) { for (final u in urls) all.add({'log': log, 'url': u}); });
  await writeStore('mils_photos', all);
  notifyListeners();
}

Future<List<String>?> pickMilsPhotos() async {
  final res = await FilePicker.platform.pickFiles(type: FileType.image, allowMultiple: true, withData: true);
  if (res == null) return null;
  return res.files.map((f) {
    if (f.bytes != null) return 'data:image/${f.extension ?? 'jpeg'};base64,${base64Encode(f.bytes!)}';
    // io fallback: read the file
    ...
  }).toList();
}
dart:io usage requires conditional import — widgets.dart is shared web+io. Simplest cross-platform: withData: true makes file_picker populate bytes on ALL platforms (it reads the file into memory). So just use bytes everywhere.

async function refreshState() {
  const s = await api(SB ? '/api/bootstrap' : '/api/state');
  products = s.products ?? [];
  customers = s.customers ?? [];
  sales = s.sales ?? [];
  invoices = s.invoices ?? [];
  txns = s.txns ?? s.transactions ?? [];
  mils = s.mils ?? s.logs ?? [];
  adjustments = s.adjustments ?? [];
  receipts = (s.receiptsIssue ?? s.receipts ?? []).map(r => ({
    ...r,
    d: r.d ?? String(r.created_at ?? '').slice(0, 10),
    amt: r.amt ?? r.amount ?? 0,
    m: r.m ?? r.method ?? 'cash',
    cust: r.cust ?? r.customer_name ?? '—',
    'for': r['for'] ?? r.source ?? '',
    by: r.by ?? r.issued_name ?? '—',
    signed: r.signed ?? r.issued_name ?? r.by ?? '—',
    contact: r.contact ?? r.customer_contact ?? '',
  }));
  docs = (s.docs ?? []).map(d => ({ ...d, type: d.type ?? d.doc_type ?? d.docType, serial: d.serial, customer: d.customer ?? d.customer_name, total: d.total ?? 0, signedBy: d.signedBy ?? d.signed_name ?? '—', date: d.date ?? d.issued_at }));
  serials = s.serials ?? serials;
  if (s.settings) settings = {
    vatEnabled: s.settings.vatEnabled ?? s.settings.vat_enabled ?? false,
    vatRate: s.settings.vatRate ?? s.settings.vat_rate ?? 0.075,
    watermark: s.settings.watermark ?? true,
  };
  rebuildMaps();
}
